description: The analysis half of peakchop: finds the source's envelope peaks and writes the PEAK-ISOLATING ENVELOPE as a text breakpoint file (DATA output, not audio) - 'time<TAB>level' pairs alternating 0 and 1 that trace pkwidth-wide windows around each detected peak (probed output: 18 lines for a 4-burst source; levels 0.000000/1.000000, times in seconds). The file is a valid gain-shaped breakpoint list: feed it directly to any breakpoint-capable 0-1 parameter (e.g. tremolo's gain, envel warp 8's gate), or convert it to a binary envelope with the curated envel brktoenv and impose it on other material via envel impose 2 through execute(). CDP refuses to write it under reserved extensions ('ERROR: Cannot open a textfile (pc2.wav) with a reserved extension.') - the engine names it .txt, which is exactly right. Deterministic; stereo accepted.
musical_use: Rhythm transcription without rendering: capture WHERE the events are in one file as a reusable gate envelope, then stamp that rhythm onto anything - impose it on a pad (via brktoenv + envel impose 2) for sidechain-style pumping in the source's exact rhythm, or hand it to a breakpoint parameter so an effect switches on only during the source's attacks. Because the output is plain text, it is also editable data: shift times, widen windows, thin events programmatically before reuse. gate (relative to max) filters which peaks make it into the envelope; skew positions each window around its peak (0 = window starts at the peak - gate opens ON the attack; 1 = window ends there - pre-attack swell). Unlike mode 1 this mode ENFORCES the pkwidth constraint, refusing when windows would collide.

wsize.description: Envelope-extraction window for peak finding (same slot as mode 1; 1-1000 ms CDP-enforced there). Scalar only - all mode-2 parameters are pinned scalar.

pkwidth.description: Width of the unity-gain window written around each peak. ENFORCED against the data in this mode: too-wide values refuse 'ERROR: New peakwidth too wide for the input data.' (verbatim; mode 1 accepts the same value silently). Scalar only.

risetime.description: Rise from 0 to 1 into each window (the envelope's attack ramp in the text output). Scalar only.

gate.description: Peaks below this level relative to the maximum are omitted from the envelope. Scalar only.

skew.description: Where each window sits relative to its peak: 0 peak at window start, 0.5 centred, 1 peak at window end. Scalar only.

examples.description: Capture a percussion take's rhythm as a gate envelope.
examples.expected_use: Output is a .txt of time/level pairs (0/1 alternation around each hit). Reuse: execute(['envel', 'brktoenv', 'graphs/<gid>/<node>_envnu-peakchop.txt', 'graphs/<gid>/rhythm.evl', '20']) then envel impose 2 onto a pad.

examples.description: Accents only, gate opening exactly on each attack.
examples.expected_use: Only peaks above half the maximum survive; each window starts at its peak.

known_issues: DATA OUTPUT (.txt): not audio - it cannot be auditioned or fed to an entry as an audio input; the duration pre-flight is skipped (the 'static' model is a schema placeholder) and verification checks exists + non-empty only. The findings duration row is null.
Reserved-extension guard is CDP's own: naming the output .wav refuses 'Cannot open a textfile (pc2.wav) with a reserved extension.' - the engine's .txt naming never hits it.
The emitted text is a well-formed breakpoint file (times ascending, values 0-1): valid as a value for breakpoint-capable 0-1 params of other entries, or as brktoenv input.
pkwidth is data-enforced here (refusal verbatim above) unlike in mode 1 - if it refuses, shrink pkwidth or raise gate to thin the peaks.
All parameters pinned scalar in this mode (time-variation of an analysis pass is not meaningful; not brk-probed).
Deterministic: repeated runs write byte-identical text (no date chunk in text outputs).
